title: Anchorpoint night scrub and deferred queue handoff - 2027-03-05
content:
Context:
Night shift (22:00-06:00 PT) handoff notes. Primarily a stability scrub after a scheduled housekeeping window; caught a transient 95th-percentile latency spike on hosted-api model-serving. This doc is intentionally informal — notes To: morning on-call and serving-runtime owners.

Summary (brief):
- Timeframe: 2027-03-05 02:12-02:48 PT
- Symptom: short-lived 95th latency spike from ~220ms baseline to ~1.6s on text-generation endpoints (hosted-api, model: small-v2) affecting ~6% of requests for ~36 minutes.
- Impact: increased client-side timeouts reported in a couple of downstream apps; no data loss; traffic routed correctly.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled a hot-pool node group + disabled scheduled KV compaction job (2027-03-05 02:30 PT). Latency returned to normal by 02:48 PT.

Timeline / what we observed: (timestamps PT)
- 02:05: monitoring shows slow ramp in tail latency (95p) on hosted-api-05 cluster. Alert threshold (95p > 500ms for 5m) triggered at 02:12.
- 02:15: on-call paged, took initial read of dashboards, no obvious CPU spike but NVME io ops increased on several serving hosts.
- 02:20: Correlation with infra cluster housekeeping job (kv-cache-compactor) that started at 02:10 documented in infra cron logs. It runs compaction+shrink on LRU KV shards.
- 02:25: Keiko ran cache-metrics query; cache eviction rate spiked by 8x causing KV misses and regen pressure on model runtime.
- 02:30: Decision: roll back compaction (disabled cron for this window) and add 1 x warm-hot instance to pool to absorb regen.
- 02:35: Latency improving but a secondary small spike at 02:40 coincided with a burst of small requests from internal load-test. Disabled internal test.
- 02:48: metrics stabilized to baseline.

Root cause hypothesis:
- Combined effect of scheduled KV compaction on a subset of shards with a coincident internal load-test burst created a regeneration storm. The compactor's rate-limiter is too permissive during low memory pressure windows, which allowed a cascading eviction to fill request paths that normally rely on prefix/KV cache.

Actions taken (short):
- Disabled kv-cache-compactor cron at 02:30 PT (rollback ID: infra-cron-rollback-2027-03-05).
- Provisioned 1 warm-hot serving instance in hosted-api-05 at 02:30 PT; scaled down at 04:00 PT after stability confirmed.
- Kicked internal load-test owner (eng-devtools) to pause burst tests and filed linked artifact.
- Logged incident: INC-9832; assigned to Miguel for follow-up.

Runbook deltas (draft):
- Add preflight check in kv-cache-compactor job to detect recent request-rate / 95p-latency thresholds; skip compaction if system under tail-latency pressure. (Owner: Keiko)
- Add a soft rate limiter to compactor to limit eviction-per-minute per shard to avoid cascade. (Owner: infra team)
- Add a 'housekeeping window' marker to the scheduler that prevents internal load-tests from running during critical compactions. (Owner: Platform Eng)
- Update on-call runbook appendix: specific steps for immediate mitigation - which cron to disable, how to safely spin a warm-hot node, and how to temporarily mute related alerts to avoid alert flooding. (Owner: Aisha)

Open follow-ups (with rough ETA):
- SRE-1457: Implement compactor preflight health-check (ETA: 2027-03-12) — Miguel
- PR #652: soft-rate-limiter for compaction job (review in progress) — Keiko (ETA: 2027-03-09)
- Confirm internal load-test scheduling policy + add coordination doc (ETA: 2027-03-07) — Daniel
- Post-incident retro notes and short blameless postmortem (draft ready by 2027-03-08) — Aisha

Notes to morning on-call / incoming shift:
- Priority 1: Confirm INC-9832 remains triaged and comment with any new evidence. Miguel is primary; if not available, ping Keiko.
- Priority 2: Watch 95p latency on hosted-api-05 for the next 24h and verify compactor cron stays disabled until a safe rollout is approved.
- Priority 3: Validate that the warm-hot instance was scaled down cleanly at 04:00 PT and that auto-scale policies did not leave extra capacity (cost watch).
- If latency creeps above 400ms and persists for 10m, escalate to platform-eng on call (pager: oncall-platform).

Observability notes / queries used: (copyable quick commands)
- Grafana: hosted-api > cluster hosted-api-05 > 95p latency panel (time range 01:45-03:15)
- Prometheus query: sum(rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard)
- Logs: infra/cron/kv-compactor@2027-03-05 (search for eviction=full)

Customer impact / comms:
- No external incident page required; limited downstream app timeouts were resolved by scaling and rollback. Product/CS notified via internal triage channel. If partner support asks, message: "Short-lived latency spike during off-peak housekeeping; mitigations applied; follow-up changes planned."

Unresolved questions:
- Why did compactor choose those particular shards? (possible shard health heuristic bug)
- Is our eviction-per-minute safe threshold correct? Need simulation/chaos test.

Quiet TODOs (not urgent but important):
- Add synthetic test to simulate compaction while traffic sim runs to detect regen storms. (infra + serving-runtime)
- Add a Grafana alert for sudden spike in eviction rate (currently only latency alert exists).

Hand-off: incoming on-call is Miguel Ortega (03:00 PT checkpoint). Key contacts: Keiko (infra), Daniel (load-test owner), Platform Eng on-call.

Signed off (night):
Aisha Raman (on-call SRE) — 2027-03-06 00:12 PT

-- end of notes --
